unstamped-pre-304.note: Inherited from the flat tests/durations.json as it stood at d49964e. No run recorded itself, so when, at what ref, at what worker count and under what load these were taken is not known and is not guessed here. Two independent reasons to distrust them as a set: tests/parallel's own docstring says they were taken under foreign load and are 3-4x too LARGE, while test_header_rule_harness.py is 10x too SMALL (25.53 recorded; 265.996s and 260.74s measured at d49964e, the very commit that wrote this file). Both cannot be true of one run. Their serial total is 1968.9s against a measured 162.4s at 8 workers = 1299 worker-seconds, so as a set they describe no run that has happened. Retained anyway: TASK-230 measured that even these produce a schedule equal to the perfect-knowledge one in three runs of four. A hint may be wrong and still useful; it may not be wrong and silent. Replace with `python3 tests/parallel --record` on a quiet machine.

never-measured.note: Listed with no number because none has ever been taken. sec:null sorts as inf, so these still run FIRST - which is what an unmentioned module already did, now by declaration instead of by omission. Being listed is what lets the drift check tell 'nobody has measured this yet' apart from 'somebody deleted the entry'; those were the same thing before TASK-304.

task-067-one-choke-point.note: Measured, not inherited and not guessed. task-276-linkage-store.note: Measured, not inherited and not guessed. Three serial runs of tests.test_linkage_store_declared with __pycache__ cleared before each - 1.34 / 1.17 / 1.20s wall, on the machine that ran TASK-276. The LARGEST is recorded, so the hint never under-books, which is the rule task-273-duplicate-ids set. load1 is high and is recorded honestly rather than waited out: five other agents were running tests/run on this machine and a quiet moment never arrived. It turned out not to matter - the three runs agree to within 0.17s, because the module's cost is 19 unittest cases and a handful of perry-lint subprocesses, not CPU. ONE CONTRARY OBSERVATION, recorded so a later reader is not surprised: the same module reported 83.9s inside a full tests/run while SIX suites at 8 workers each were competing. That is a contention figure, not this module's cost, and it is named here rather than averaged in - a number that folds two regimes together describes neither.

task-278-linkage-readers.note: Measured, not inherited and not guessed. The spread here is wider than that row's - 1.10s across three runs against its 0.30 - and the reason is worth recording rather than averaging away: this module spawns perry-lint over a fixture project 12 times, and perry-lint's cost is dominated by reading schema/state-schema.json and walking the tree, so it is more sensitive to page cache than to CPU. The first run after a cold cache is the fast one here only because the largest run happened to land on a load spike. Expect a much larger figure inside a full tests/run at 8 workers; that is a contention figure and not this module's cost.
